notes.text: Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin.

Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 42:47 together, about what it had with Määttä (48%).
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, down from 34% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 53:12 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Kiefer Sherwood is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games.
Jacob Trouba is out (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Michael Kesselring is expected back after missing 1 game.
Brett Leason was added to the roster on Nov 18 and has played beside Barclay Goodrow and Zack Ostapchuk.

SJS.head: The Sharks face a real test
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage and Minnesota will be without Hughes, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

MIN.head: The Wild should have the upper hand
MIN.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage and Minnesota will be without Hughes, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Celebrini’s favorite opponent
paras: The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Minnesota on Nov 6. The Wild (17-3-5) lost 4-3 in a shootout to Vancouver on Saturday, while the Sharks (11-12-2) beat Seattle 4-3 the same night. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (tied for first in the NHL) and the Sharks third in the Pacific (tied for 19th).

The Wild’s record (.780) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.639), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Sharks’ (.480 on chances worth .404), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Wild have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.20 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (30th). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Kirill Kaprizov (18 G / 27 A / 45 P in 25 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with 13 points in his last five games and eight goals in nine games against San Jose since 2023-24. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (10 G / 19 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Minnesota.
Filip Gustavsson is expected to start for Minnesota, his first start of the season, and Yaroslav Askarov (6-9-1 / .888 SV% in 16 GS) for San Jose.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.
